newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may amend draft De Beers gem deal - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia may amend draft De Beers gem deal - minister.

text.p: Russia may amend the draft of a long-delayed trade agreement with De Beers, Interfax news agency on Tuesday quoted Finance Minister Alexander Livshits as saying.

Livshits, quoted as telling workers at a diamond processing plant in Smolensk that the facility needed a steady supply of rough diamonds, said: "Naturally, we should take this condition into consideration when preparing those changes which will have to be brought into the draft trade agreement with De Beers."

Livshits was quoted as saying that the changes, which he did not specify, "should not encourage the re-export of diamonds, but should only provide adequate supplies for existing production capacities (to process diamonds) in Russia."
He said the Russian government had no doubt about the necessity of signing a trade agreement with De Beers.

A draft agreement based on a February memorandum with the South African gem corporation was recently presented to the Russian cabinet after undergoing analysis in various ministries. But the Russian government has yet to approve the document.
Livshits was speaking at the Kristall diamond processing plant, the largest facility of its kind in Russia and capable, he said, of processing at least $550 million worth of rough gems a year.
The official Itar-Tass news agency quoted Livshits as saying he could give no date for the signing of a deal with De Beers "since we will have to work meticulously on a new document".
Russian gem and government officials have said repeatedly that they are keen to see the domestic cutting and polishing industry grow and for greater supplies of gems to stay in Russia for processing.
Russia, through Almazy Rossii-Sakha, or ARS, supplies about one quarter of De Beers output.

ARS officials have said that under the February memorandum, ARS would have the right to export $180 million of gems a year independent of De Beers, or 5.8 percent of ARS's $1.38 billion in sales last year.

But delay in finalising the deal has created uncertainty in the world diamond market. De Beers is keen for tighter control over the "leakage" of Russian gems onto world markets outside trade agreements.
